anomaly_def.Name: Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the operating-system kernel and per-process resource-limit layer, where database processes, sessions, or background workers exhaust limits enforced by the host kernel rather than by the database engine itself. It is distinct from database memory, CPU, storage, and network anomalies because the limiting resource is a kernel-managed object such as file handles, shared memory segments, semaphores, message queues, asynchronous-I/O contexts, process or thread quotas, virtual address ranges, or namespace and cgroup quotas. Observable phenomena: engine errors referring to inability to open files, allocate shared memory, create threads, or acquire kernel synchronization primitives, kernel-reported denials of resource allocation visible in system message logs, intermittent failures of new sessions or background workers despite database-level slots being available, sudden inability to spawn parallel workers, and partial outages where the engine continues to serve existing work but cannot expand. Possible contributing factors: overly conservative per-process file-handle, locked-memory, or stack-size limits, kernel-level shared-memory or semaphore caps left at default values, virtual-memory or address-space configuration insufficient for the engine footprint, asynchronous-I/O context limits saturated by parallel workers, process or thread quotas reached after connection bursts, container or cgroup memory and process-id limits reached, and orphaned resources (handles, shared segments, semaphores) accumulating after abnormal terminations.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle, but not within an open transaction, for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle and not inside an open transaction longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; the documentation warns about using this with connection pools or middleware.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
